issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Rideable.messageOnRide() as a no-argument method returning a String (and the instructions expect the return value "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"), and the template Main uses r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. However, the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (and implementing classes Pig and Seal implement messageOnRide(int speed)). This parameter mismatch between the specification/template and the solution will confuse students and break the expected usage in Main and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable.messageOnRide signature across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to match the problem/template by making Rideable.messageOnRide() a no-argument method returning String, and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if an integer speed parameter is intended, update the problem statement, UML, template Main usage, and instructions to declare and use messageOnRide(int speed) consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement defines Rideable.messageOnRide() as a no-argument method returning a String (and specifies the return format "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). The solution repository declares Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (an int parameter) and Pig/Seal implement this signature and include the speed in the returned text ("at X mph"). The template Main also calls messageOnRide() with no arguments. This mismatch in method signature and expected return value creates a direct mapping confusion: students are instructed to implement/use a no-arg messageOnRide(), but the solution uses a different signature and behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable API across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change solution's Rideable to declare String messageOnRide() (no parameters) and update Pig and Seal implementations to return "Riding on [AnimalType] [name]" (remove speed and "at X mph"). Also ensure template Main calls and any documentation use the no-arg form. Alternatively, if speed is desired, update the problem statement and template to require messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust the expected return format accordingly.
